chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Why Shaw's Boston band could not play "Traffic Jam"
summary: Shaw's band could not handle it, so he rebuilt his band before recording the hit version.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: If I write an arrangement or something, you know, like when I wrote "Traffic Jam" for Artie -- the band that Artie had in Boston, the band couldn't play it.
Artie came to me and say, "Look, this" -- he rehearsed with that band. He say, "I can't play this. I'll do it later when I get to New York, because I'm going to change my band around."
That's when he Georgie Auld. A few of the other trombone players came in there, (inaudible), put some other men in his band.
He called me up from Detroit and say, "I'm gonna play you "Traffic Jam.""
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
When he says he's going to play it, he played it. That's the "Traffic Jam" you hear on the record. It was out of sight.
Now when he rehearsed it in Boston, his band couldn't play it. He couldn't get out of what he wanted out of the band.
The brass couldn't do what they want -- you know, couldn't put it over.
